chapter: Chicago boyhood and the Austin High Gang
title: The eight blind men singing spirituals: his first jazz feeling
summary: The brothers hear and pass the hat for blind street musicians playing swinging spirituals, which he calls his first influence.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: But you were talking about the influences though in this particular mixed neighborhood.

Ah, here's what happened. Now my brother and I had always played violin and I had played a little bit of the peck horn, and he played E-flat alto horn, in my father's band at picnics and things. It was a regular band you know, marching band style, that kind of stuff. And so forth.

And so I had musical training already. Now one night, it was a mixed neighborhood as I say, on Lake and Polina Lincoln Street on the West Side of Chicago. And there were eight colored men, blind colored men who heard this music across the street. Two or three basses and banjos and a guitar, mandolin and guitar. And they were singing spirituals. Gospel music. And my brother and I were, let me preface this by saying this. We were tough little monkeys in those days. Rough kids, you know, that's a tough neighborhood. And we would steal everything we could lay our hands on. We were bad.

Had a gang and everything else. Hermitage Gang.
So we could hear this music and go over to see these

eight guys and blind, all blind and playing this music which was really something. They were playing spirituals and it's swinging. It's rocking, it's going. And my God, my brother and I just flipped man. They're singing and the band is, you know, these spirituals.

And my brother and I started passing the hat for them and the people started putting the money in the hat for them and everything like that, and we gave them every penny. You can imagine, that was a compliment to them. (LAUGHTER). They must have been good because we loved them and we didn't even steal one penny from them.

We passed the hat for them. We got all this money and kept giving it to the guys there you know. And they were thanking us. But we'd listen, and they used to come a couple of times a week and play. But they were really the spirituals. I don't mean ....... ............(IMITATES SOUND OF SPIRITUALS).... ...
Oh, (you've got a good bass in there haven't you?)?
Well man, it was swinging and that's where we really got our first feeling for we could call it jazz. But gospel music, spiritual music, that was it.
